stubs.angle: A request carries a valid token, but the user lacks permission for the resource: which status code should the API return?
stubs.answerHinge: 403 Forbidden means the server understood the credentials and refuses; 401 Unauthorized means credentials are missing or invalid and must come with a WWW-Authenticate challenge.

stubs.angle: A runnable snippet with a stub handler that returns 404 and a text body parses the body as data and fails; find the line that skips the status check.
stubs.answerHinge: HttpClient.GetAsync returns a response for any status code and never throws on 4xx or 5xx, so the code must check IsSuccessStatusCode or call EnsureSuccessStatusCode before reading the body.

stubs.angle: A client posts an application/xml body to an endpoint that only accepts JSON: which status code fits?
stubs.answerHinge: 415 Unsupported Media Type is about the format of the request content, while 406 Not Acceptable is about the Accept header and the response format.

stubs.angle: Which of the listed changes to an existing API version break clients that are already integrated?
stubs.answerHinge: Removing or renaming a field, changing a field type and making an optional input required are breaking, while adding an optional response field or an optional input is not.

stubs.angle: Why is an endpoint such as GET /orders/42/cancel dangerous even when only logged-in users can call it?
stubs.answerHinge: RFC 9110 defines GET as safe, so crawlers, link prefetchers, caches and automatic retries may issue it without user intent, and any state change it makes is triggered unintentionally.

stubs.angle: How do you stop two clients that PUT the same resource from silently overwriting each other's changes at the HTTP level?
stubs.answerHinge: The server sends an ETag, the client sends it back in If-Match, and the server rejects a stale write with 412 Precondition Failed (and can demand the header with 428 Precondition Required).

stubs.angle: A list endpoint with page and pageSize slows down on deep pages and shows duplicates while data is inserted: how would you redesign pagination?
stubs.answerHinge: Offset pagination makes the database skip rows and shifts pages under inserts, while cursor (keyset) pagination seeks from an opaque continuation token on an indexed key, giving stable and fast pages at the cost of jumping to an arbitrary page.

stubs.angle: Which exception does a .NET 5+ HttpClient throw when HttpClient.Timeout elapses, and how do you tell it apart from caller cancellation?
stubs.answerHinge: It throws TaskCanceledException whose InnerException is TimeoutException, while a cancellation requested by the caller shows up as the caller's token having IsCancellationRequested set.

stubs.angle: A service downloads large files with GetAsync and then ReadAsStreamAsync, yet memory grows by the file size: what fixes it?
stubs.answerHinge: The default HttpCompletionOption.ResponseContentRead buffers the whole body before GetAsync completes, so you must pass ResponseHeadersRead, stream the content and dispose the response.

stubs.angle: In an ASP.NET Core registration and service class, find the line that makes a typed HttpClient keep calling an old address after a DNS switch.
stubs.answerHinge: Typed clients are registered as transient, and injecting one into a singleton pins a single HttpMessageHandler for the process lifetime, so IHttpClientFactory never rotates the handler.

stubs.angle: Which statements about AddStandardResilienceHandler from Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience are true for outgoing POST requests?
stubs.answerHinge: By default the standard pipeline retries transient failures for every HTTP method including POST, and DisableForUnsafeHttpMethods is needed to stop retries of POST, PATCH, PUT, DELETE and CONNECT.

stubs.angle: After v2 shipped and DefaultApiVersion was set to 2.0 with AssumeDefaultVersionWhenUnspecified, clients that never send a version started failing: what happened and what do you change?
stubs.answerHinge: The assumed default applies to every request without a version, so moving it silently migrates unversioned clients; the default must stay on the oldest supported version or the version must be required explicitly.

stubs.angle: How do you decide whether your teams write the OpenAPI contract first or generate it from the ASP.NET Core code?
stubs.answerHinge: Design-first makes the contract a reviewed artifact that consumers agree on before implementation and that CI can diff for breaking changes, while code-first is faster but lets the contract drift with implementation details.

stubs.angle: During a slowdown of a downstream API its traffic multiplied, and each of three services in the call chain retries three times: what do you change and how do you make it a team rule?
stubs.answerHinge: Retries at every layer multiply attempts (3 x 3 x 3), so retrying belongs to one layer with a total timeout budget, a circuit breaker and respect for Retry-After.

stubs.angle: Ten services return errors in ten different shapes and clients parse message text: how do you standardize the error contract?
stubs.answerHinge: Adopt RFC 9457 Problem Details everywhere with stable type URIs or error codes that clients branch on, keep detail for humans only, and enforce the shape with shared configuration and contract tests.

stubs.angle: Hundreds of partners want push notifications about order changes instead of polling: how do you design outbound webhooks that stay reliable for years?
stubs.answerHinge: Webhooks are at-least-once deliveries from a durable queue, so each event needs a unique id for receiver deduplication and a signature, with backoff retries and per-endpoint isolation so one slow partner cannot delay the others.
